result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide multi-lane intersection situated beneath a massive elevated rail structure. Large steel support columns create significant visual obstructions and physical barriers on the sidewalks, while the lack of medians or curb extensions results in long, unprotected crossing distances for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Elevated Rail Columns
hazards.description: Large steel support columns are located at the edge of the sidewalk and roadway, creating significant blind spots for both drivers and pedestrians at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Positioned along the curb line on both sides of the street and at the intersection corners.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a significant distance without a refuge island, increasing exposure to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway and Lehigh Av.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the corners to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers by moving the waiting area past the rail columns.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a median or refuge island in the center of the wide roadway to allow pedestrians to cross in two stages.

interventions.title: Enhanced Under-Structure Lighting
interventions.description: Improve lighting specifically under the elevated rail structure to eliminate dark spots and improve personal security and visibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a large elevated rail structure whose support columns create significant visual obstructions at the intersection. While sidewalks and marked crosswalks are present, the space feels constrained and visibility between drivers and pedestrians is compromised by the infrastructure.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Infrastructure
hazards.description: Large steel support columns for the elevated rail line significantly block sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching vehicles.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bins and utility poles narrow the effective walking width of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side sidewalk near the buildings

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to move pedestrians into the line of sight of drivers beyond the support columns and shorten the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Enhanced Under-Structure Lighting
interventions.description: Improve lighting levels beneath the elevated rail structure to increase the visibility of pedestrians, especially during dawn, dusk, or overcast conditions.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearance
interventions.description: Relocate trash bins and other movable obstructions to maintain a clear, consistent walking path.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by an elevated rail structure, which creates significant visual obstructions due to large support pillars. While sidewalks are present, the lack of marked crossings and the presence of blank building frontages contribute to a less-than-ideal environment for walking.

hazards.name: Pillar sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Large steel support pillars for the elevated rail structure block visibility between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left-center of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked crossing points for pedestrians across the roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate safe crossing locations.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond the pillars.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting fixtures directed at the sidewalk to improve safety and security under the dark overhead structure.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a massive elevated steel structure whose support columns significantly obstruct the sidewalk. While a paved walkway exists, the presence of blank fencing and physical obstructions creates a confined and potentially hazardous space for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Physical Obstruction
hazards.description: Large blue steel support columns for the elevated structure are positioned directly in the sidewalk, severely narrowing the effective walking path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right foreground, occupying the sidewalk area.

hazards.name: Visual Blind Spots
hazards.description: The massive scale of the steel columns and the opaque fencing create significant blind spots, reducing visibility between pedestrians and potential vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk where the columns meet the ground.

hazards.name: Trip Hazards
hazards.description: Cracked pavement and vegetation growth in the sidewalk joints indicate poor maintenance and present minor trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Lower left and center, at the base of the steel structure.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-quality lighting underneath the elevated structure to improve visibility and personal security in the shadowed area.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Delineation and Repair
interventions.description: Repair the cracked pavement and use high-visibility markings or different paving textures to clearly define the pedestrian path around the obstructions.

interventions.title: Frontage Improvement
interventions.description: Replace the blank chain-link and mesh fencing with more transparent or aesthetically pleasing barriers to improve 'eyes on the street'.
